Ask: which sorting algorithm does the fixture's `sort.rs` implement, and what is its worst case? - wanted: the algorithm and its worst-case complexity.
For you: it implements quicksort, and the worst case is O(n^2). I made no edits and ran no tests.
Now: done.
Next: nothing.

**Algorithm.** `src/sort.rs` in the fixture (`/home/projects/ulwbench-home/tmp-base/ulw-bench-S6-r1-MieKiI/`) implements in-place recursive quicksort with the Lomuto partition scheme (`quicksort` at lines 7-15, `partition` at lines 17-28).

**Worst case: O(n^2) time.** The pivot is always the last element (`arr[len - 1]`, line 21), with no randomization and no median-of-three. On already-sorted, reverse-sorted, or all-equal input, each partition peels off only one element. That gives n levels of recursion, each doing a linear scan.
- All-equal input is also quadratic here. `<=` on line 21 sends every element to the left side.
- The doc comment at lines 3-6 states the same bounds. It says average and best case are O(n log n).

**Space.** Beyond the O(n) time, the worst-case recursion depth is also O(n) stack frames. The code recurses on both halves and never recurses on the smaller side first. Sorted or all-equal input of large size could therefore overflow the stack.

I did not run the code. This comes from reading the source.

I skipped the ulw-research team, skills, goal, notepad and tier steps because this was a single-file read-only question. The answer was already in hand, so those steps would have added no evidence.
